questions.q: Besides a stack of TransformerBlocks, which four pieces does a decoder-only transformer add?
options: Token embedding, positional embedding, a final LayerNorm, and a linear head to vocab logits
Two extra attention heads, a dropout layer, a softmax, and a second embedding table
A convolutional layer, batch normalization, a pooling layer, and a classifier head
An encoder stack, cross-attention, a decoder stack, and a final softmax
questions.explain: TinyGPT wraps the block stack with token embedding, positional embedding, one final LayerNorm, and a Linear(d_model, vocab_size) head producing logits.

questions.q: Given `mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(T, T), diagonal=1).bool()`, what does `mask[i, j] == True` mean?
options: Position j is in the past relative to position i, and should be attended to
Position j is strictly in the future relative to position i (j > i), and attention should be blocked there
Position i and j are the same token
The mask entry is always False for every i, j
questions.explain: torch.triu with diagonal=1 keeps the strict upper triangle, so mask[i, j] is True exactly when j > i — a future position — which attn_mask then blocks.

questions.q: Why does `TinyGPT.forward` store its transformer blocks in `nn.ModuleList` rather than a plain Python list?
options: A plain list would raise a syntax error in Python
nn.ModuleList is required to compute the causal mask
nn.ModuleList correctly registers each block's parameters so PyTorch tracks and trains them
There is no difference; it's purely a style choice
questions.explain: nn.ModuleList makes PyTorch aware of the submodules so their parameters show up in .parameters() and get updated during training. A plain Python list would hide them from the optimizer.

questions.q: For input `idx` of shape (B, T), what is the shape of `TinyGPT.forward(idx)`'s return value?
options: (B, d_model)
(B, T, d_model)
(B, T, vocab_size)
(T, vocab_size)
questions.explain: The final nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size) head projects every position's d_model vector to a vocab_size score vector, giving a final shape of (B, T, vocab_size).

questions.q: What does passing `is_causal=True` to `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` accomplish, compared to building a mask with `torch.triu` and passing `attn_mask`?
options: It disables attention masking entirely
It produces equivalent causal masking behavior without needing to materialize an explicit mask tensor
It only works for positional embeddings, not attention
It changes the model from decoder-only to encoder-decoder
questions.explain: is_causal=True handles causal masking internally, achieving the same effect as an explicit torch.triu-built boolean mask, typically more conveniently and efficiently.
